messages:
kim: Quick spike proposal 1: split tokenizer/encoding out of runtime into a standalone TokenService to reduce duplicate tokenization work and make quantization compatibility testable. thinking of it as a small service with a stable proto surface.
kim: Rationale: multiple runtimes currently implement slightly different tokenization quirks (leading whitespace, fallback unknown tokens) causing drift in evals and making cross-runtime canaries noisy. also heavy CPU on hotpath for short prompts.
arjun: totally. any perf numbers yet? do we expect net latency win vs added network hop?
kim: ballpark: naive tokenization is ~1-2ms per request on our infra but we see 200k rps of short prompts -> that adds up. if we cache and centralize, we can save duplicate work and share a warmed tokenizer; network hop + batching may be cheaper overall. need benchmark spike.
maya: depends on batching semantics. if TokenService supports multi-request batching & TTLed encodings we can amortize cost. but watch tail latency for interactive flows.
jules: tradeoffs: more infra complexity, more things to deploy, but tighter hermetic contract and easier QA of quantized tokenizers. Also helps us adopt tokenizer fixes across fleets.
samira: migration concerns: session mutation ordering, and KV cache keys currently assume runtime internal token ids. If we change encoding, we need a migration adapter that can translate cached keys or support dual-read during ramp.
kim: propose interface (proto) for TokenService:
```
service TokenService {
  rpc Encode(EncodeRequest) returns (EncodeResponse);
  rpc Decode(DecodeRequest) returns (DecodeResponse);
}
message EncodeRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string model_spec = 2;
  bytes text = 3;
  bool allow_partial = 4;
}
message EncodeResponse {
  repeated int32 token_ids = 1;
  string tokenizer_v = 2;
}
```
kim: include tokenizer_v so runtimes can opt-in per-request and we can route by compatibility.
arjun: For rollout, I like a proxying approach: runtime calls TokenService but with a local hot-cache fallback. Start with local-first read then async backfill to TokenService, then flip to central-first. That reduces immediate blast radius.
maya: tests: collect canonical tokenization cases (unicode, emojis, long prefixes, adversarial whitespace). gate on bit-exact encodings for critical models. store them in eval-harness.
jules: perf plan: 1) microbench tokenization in-process vs through local proxy with batch window sizes (1ms, 5ms, 10ms). 2) run a synthetic short-prompt workload. 3) measure p50/p95 end-to-end increase.
samira: compatibility: define migration TTL for cache keys and a reconciliation worker. The worker will map old-key -> new-key for sessions created in the overlap window. Also keep a deprecation window of 8 weeks.
kim: ops: add checklist "token-service-unbundle" with steps for baseline snapshot, staged canaries, and metrics to watch (encode.latency.p50/p95, token-cache-hit, token-mismatch-rate).
ops-bot: deploybot: created checklist "token-service-unbundle" assigned to kim and ops-engineering. link: https://deploy/redwood/checklists/token-service-unbundle
arjun: QA fuzz: create a tokenizer-fuzzer that validates decode(encode(x)) == x for a corpus and flags any mismatch. Also deterministic seed for tokenization RNGs.
maya: security: tokenization can leak prompts in logs if not careful. adapters must mark traces as pii and redact where appropriate. add a redact flag on EncodeRequest for telemetry.
kim: example shim config for runtime proxy:
```
proxy:
  local_cache_size: 1_000_000
  batch_window_ms: 5
  token_service_endpoint: https://token-service.internal:8080
headers:
  - x-rw-tokenizer-version
```
kim: within cut we run shadow-encodes to compare local vs service encodings and measure mismatch rate before any traffic flipping.
jules: cost: product should be aware we'll add a small infra tax (extra service), but likely net CPU savings across fleet. include a cost model in the RFC.
samira: ops note: plan a trace-day and bump ingestion retention to 72h for the stabilize window so we can investigate mismatches in detail.
arjun: ownership: propose infra eng owns TokenService; runtime teams own their proxy integration. pair a runtime eng with infra for tranche 1.
kim: timeline suggestion: discovery spike (2w) to prove perf and mismatch rates, cut (6w) for proxy + token-service alpha, stabilize (2w) for canary and reconcile. mirror the debt tranche cadence.
maya: add success criteria: mismatch-rate < 0.05% on core prompt set, p95 E2E latency increase < 5ms for interactive routes, token-cache-hit > 80% after warmup.
samira: fallback: if mismatch > threshold we abort and fall back to local tokenization. add automatic rollback trigger.
ops-bot: deploybot: checklist updated: add step "capture snapshot: tokenizer-baseline-metrics".
kim: next steps: I'll open the repo-level RFC + benchmark plan. @arjun @maya volunteer to co-own validation?
arjun: I'll co-own validation harness and perf spike.
maya: I'll help with rollout and telemetry hooks.
jules: :thumbsup: ping me if product needs cost numbers.
kim: thanks all. i'll post the RFC draft by Friday and link the scoring sheet. plan to discuss at Mon arch sync.
